summary: John Muir studied at the University of Glasgow, East India Company College, Fort William College, and the University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1844), and held a post at the University of Edinburgh.

Working in religious studies and Indology, John Murdoch studied at the High School of Glasgow and the University of Glasgow (LL.D. ~1878). He served as Agent and Travelling Secretary for the Christian Vernacular Education Society (1858–1903) and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.

Indologist and religious studies scholar John Murray Mitchell studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, Marischal College, Aberdeen, the University of Aberdeen, and the University of Edinburgh. He taught at Wilson College, Mumbai (1844–1866) and served as Principal of Duff College (1868–1873).

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, John Myrdhin Reynolds studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Rinpoche (~1971–1987), Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (~1979), and Namkhai Norbu. He also founded the Bonpo Translation Project.

Working in religious studies and Indology, John N. Carpenter was a missionary for the Church Mission Society. He served as Principal of St. Paul's Divinity School (1900) and Emmanuel College (1916–1922), and held a post at St. John's College, Agra.

Working in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, John Nemec earned degrees from the University of Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn (PhD 2005), studying under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher. In 2004, he became Associate Professor at the University of Virginia.

A linguist, John Okell studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg (~1960–1963). From 1959 to 1999, he served as a research associate at SOAS University of London.

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, John P. Keenan earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota (attested 1980) and studied under Noriaki Hakamaya. He was a research fellow at Nanzan University (1983–1986) and later taught at Middlebury College.

Indologist and linguist John Peile studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, and the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. At Cambridge, he became Reader of Comparative Philology (1884–1893) and Master of Christ's College (1887), later serving as President of Newnham College (~1890–1909).

John Penry Lewis, who worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, completed his B.A. at Queen's University Belfast in 1876. He served as a civil servant in the Ceylon Civil Service from 1877 to 1910.

Specializing in religious studies and Indology, John Peter Jones studied at Case Western Reserve University and Andover Theological Seminary. He served as Principal of Pasumalai Seminary (1892–1914) and Professor of Indian Missions at Hartford Seminary (1914).
John Peter Wade was an Indologist and historian who studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh. In 1784, he served as an Assistant Medical Surgeon for the East India Company.

Indologist John Pickford studied at Brasenose College and the University of Oxford under Monier Monier-Williams. He held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai (until 1872) and as Professor at the University of Madras.

Active in Indology and other fields, John Playfair studied at the University of St Andrews, St Mary's College, and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Professor of Mathematics at Edinburgh (1785–1818) and co-founded the Royal Society of Edinburgh in 1783.

Scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, John Powers earned his doctorate at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. His posts include a chair at the Australian National University (1995–2016), Research Professor at Deakin University (2016–2022), and lecturer at the University of Melbourne (2022).

Working in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, John R. B. Campbell completed his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb. He also studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Denma Lochö Rinpoche, and Lobsang Ngawang.

Scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology John R. McRae completed his PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Cornell, Indiana University Bloomington (~1995–2006), Soka University (2004), and Komazawa University (~2005–2009).
A scholar in Buddhist studies, John Riley Perks was taught by traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, John Ronald Newman received his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa (1987). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1987) and New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

Scholar of Buddhist and religious studies John Ross Carter studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wilfred Cantwell Smith. He served as a professor at Colgate University and its Chapel House from around 1972 to 2006.
